about: D42 (decision log): the paired, interleaved confirmation that is the verdict on "no latency regression", on the scaling report's 300,000-patient snapshot (the kept D34 build, reused unchanged), by tools/benchmark_matcher.py --paired-confirm (protocol paired-interleaved-1.0) into a scratch report and committed here as it was written. The reference is main before D42 (f99e4f9, extracted from git); the candidate is this tree, whose files the artifact digests bind. The matcher comparison report is not regenerated (nothing it binds changed). The confirmation queries carry no joint (gene steps under coded only), gene or coded-only request, so this measures only the path of requests that are not joint; execution_store.py, the engine and store_conditions_relative.py are byte-identical in the two codes. Latency of joint requests at scale is not measured.
rule: No latency regression: at 14 workers the paired p95 ratio (candidate over reference) is at most 1.05 in every pair, and the candidate's own 14-worker p95 is at most 10 s; the maximum, memory and 8 workers are reported (committed in 72c8091).

paired_confirmation.order: ABBA: the reference first in even repeats, the candidate first in odd

budget_policy.name: engine-default
budget_policy.description: every query's search_budget is 40,000: the engine's default when the field is absent and what every shipped client sends (the trajectory page, the store query page, the request examples). The query is random_query's draw with only search_budget replaced (D41).

paired_confirmation.note: Each pair is the reference code and the candidate code run back to back, each in a fresh process with a warm pool, on the same snapshot and queries, each at the search budget policy its side states (budget_policy, D41); the reference runs first in even repeats and second in odd ones (ABBA). Ratios are candidate over reference: below 1 means the candidate is faster. "total" is the sum of the per-query match seconds of one run. The absolute target is judged on the candidate's own runs in this session. The pairing cancels drift that is slow against the length of a pair (minutes); it does not cancel noise within a run, nor a difference that only one order shows (compare the reference-first and candidate-first pairs).

limitations: one machine and one session; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients; the p95 of 30 queries is the second-slowest query; the paired protocol cancels slow drift, not noise inside a run; no joint request is timed
